title: How to Run Embedded Payments at Scale: ACH Rails, Payouts and Operations
partialText: Running embedded payments at scale means managing returns, reconciliation, compliance and payouts continuously, and the work grows with transaction volume. Dwolla by NMI has operated that layer for more than 16 years. Client results include $700 million in earnest money processed without a fraud incident, an 800% gain in reimbursement efficiency and 80% fewer cashout support tickets.

title: The Biggest Mistake Platform Teams Make Is Hiding Complexity
partialText: The article argues that platform teams often mistake abstraction for simplicity, hiding critical system behaviors instead of exposing them responsibly. Through examples spanning cloud platforms, microservices, low-code tools, and data pipelines, it advocates designing abstractions that preserve observability, expose failure modes, and retain developer control, making distributed systems more resilient under real-world conditions.

title: NetNut Shut Down by the FBI? Here’s What Happened and What to Do Next
partialText: FBI disruption of NetNut reshapes proxy industry standards, highlighting compliance and governance. Explore what happened and what you should consider when evaluating a NetNut alternative.

title: The User Is the Content
partialText: AI can generate expertise at scale, making it less of a competitive advantage. The article argues that firsthand experience, user-generated content, and proprietary data are becoming the signals that search engines and AI systems increasingly value, pushing content teams to automate routine work while investing more heavily in authentic human insight.

title: How Cloud Controls Frameworks and Agentic AI Simplify Compliance and Accelerate Market Access
partialText: The article explains how organizations can reduce compliance duplication by building a Cloud Controls Framework (CCF) that maps common controls across multiple security and AI governance standards. It also explores how AI agents can automate evidence collection, control mapping, gap analysis, and questionnaire responses while supporting newer frameworks such as ISO/IEC 42001, the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, and AIUC-1.

title: TALOS Wants to Break AI's Cloud Monopoly, One GPU at a Time
partialText: The article introduces TALOS, a decentralized AI inference network that connects idle consumer GPUs into a peer-to-peer compute marketplace. It explains how contributors can monetize unused hardware, how developers can access distributed AI models, and why the project sees decentralization as an alternative to hyperscale AI infrastructure.

title: Why Cybersecurity Governance Depends on Decisions, Not Just Controls
partialText: The article argues that cybersecurity maturity depends on more than documented controls and compliance frameworks. As organizations become more complex, maintaining visibility into the reasoning behind security decisions becomes critical for governance, accountability, and long-term resilience, particularly in regulated environments.

title: ISP Traffic Shaping: Why Your Streaming Buffers Even When Your Internet Seems Fine
partialText: The article explains how ISPs use deep packet inspection (DPI) and traffic classification to identify and selectively throttle bandwidth-intensive services such as streaming platforms. It also explores how VPNs obscure destination information, reducing the effectiveness of selective throttling, while clarifying the limitations of encryption and offering practical ways to detect whether throttling is occurring.

title: Why AI Agent Cost Attribution Has to Be Per Task
partialText: AI agents don't generate costs one API call at a time—they incur costs across complex, multi-step tasks involving models, tools, retries, and workflows. Event-level dashboards hide unprofitable workloads, while per-task attribution reveals true margins, supports sustainable pricing, and enables real-time cost control. As agentic AI scales, task-level economics are becoming essential for profitability.

title: Breach At The Beach: The Ultimate Entra ID Training Experience
partialText: Breach at the Beach is a free Capture the Flag (CTF) built by Varonis Threat Labs to teach defenders how modern attackers abuse Microsoft Entra ID. Based on real-world investigations, it covers non-human identities, AI-driven attack paths, identity-based data exfiltration, and threat detection through hands-on challenges. Players earn CPE credits while developing practical skills for defending today's cloud-first environments.

title: Is the Traditional Career Ladder Becoming a Lattice?
partialText: The traditional career ladder is giving way to the career lattice, where growth happens through lateral moves, reskilling, and cross-functional experience—not just promotions. This article explores why flatter organizations, changing workforce expectations, and transferable business skills are redefining career success, while examining the benefits and challenges of building a career that moves in multiple directions instead of only upward.

title: EvilTokens: How “Ghost” Code Threatens US and European Businesses
partialText: EvilTokens conceals its phishing workflow behind browser-side AES-GCM decryption, making static URL analysis insufficient for detecting Microsoft 365 device code attacks. This article shows how browser-level inspection in ANY.RUN reveals decrypted pages, traces device-code phishing activity, uncovers related infrastructure through threat intelligence, and helps SOC teams investigate, detect, and contain attacks faster.
